summary: You need the six CHEMENG core courses, 3 units of CHEMENG 699 colloquium and 24 more units of graduate lecture courses (numbered 200 and above, at least 3 units each), with 90 graduate units in all, research included. Every course must be letter graded when a letter grade is offered. You check by hand that the curriculum committee chair and department chair approve your extra lecture courses, the 3.0 GPA, the reading committee meeting by your ninth quarter and the thesis.

program.why: Grading: "Any course intended to satisfy the Engineer degree requirements must be taken for a letter grade, if offered." The research, teaching and colloquium courses are offered only S/NC. The Bulletin's own 90-unit minimum is now in the data.

add.why: GPA: "An overall grade point average (GPA) of 3.0 must be maintained."

"a minimum of 45 units in science and engineering courses, consisting of 42 lecture units and 3 CHEMENG 699 Colloquium units" (the six core courses carry 18) and "The additional lecture courses, (24 units), may be chosen from graduate level science and engineering courses ... the course work may not include chemical engineering's 500 level seminar courses or similar 1-2 unit courses in other departments." Research and teaching units are left out; that a course is science or engineering is part of the committee consent (ov-lecture-consent).
"with the consent of the graduate curriculum committee chair and the department chair"

node.name: Additional lecture courses approved by the curriculum committee chair and department chair

add.why: "All candidates are required to have an initial meeting with their reading committees by the end of their ninth quarter."

add.why: "The thesis must represent a substantial piece of research equivalent to nine months of full-time effort and must be approved by the student's reading committee."
